BioWordVec, an open set of pre-trained biomedical word embeddings, can significantly outperform the state of the art word embeddings in multiple biomedical text mining tasks, especially when combined with MeSH information.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and evaluation of a novel approach to generating biomedical word embeddings, which combines subword information with a controlled biomedical vocabulary.

the development of novel and efficient machine learning algorithms to improve the quality and performance of the word representations, which are widely used in the biomedical natural language processing and information retrieval.
developing and assessing a novel word embedding method that incorporates both subword information and domain specific structured information.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
BioWordVec word vectors are a useful tool for improving the performance of many BioNLP tasks.
BioWordVec is an open source word embedding that can improve the performance of many NLP tasks in biomedical domain.

BioWordVec, which is the first publicly available biomedical word embedding trained with subword information, is a significant advance over the previous state-of-the-art biomedical word embeddings, and can be used for a variety of biomedical NLP tasks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have generated a set of word embeddings that combine both the subword information present in biomedical text and the MeSH vocabulary, which is widely used in biomedical text mining and information extraction, and we have shown that our generated embeddings can significantly improve performance in multiple challenging biomedical NLP tasks.
we have generated a new set of word vectors/embeddings for biomedical text, which are based on the combination of subword and MeSH information.

we have developed a new set of biomedical word embeddings that combines subword and MeSH information and demonstrated that they can improve performance over multiple NLP benchmarks in the biomedical domain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of subword and ontology information can significantly improve the quality of biomedical word vectors.
the combination of subword information from a large unlabeled corpus with domain specific structured information can greatly improve the quality of the biomedical word representation.
word representations can be greatly improved by leveraging subword information from both unlabeled and labeled text.
